source.display_title: 05/04/2026 - Jaideep  Mistry x Farooq Bey — Follow Up

prospect.name: Paul Hatch
prospect.location: West Sussex, England, UK — about an hour from London
prospect.occupation: Chef and business owner. Runs a mobile catering business and is two to three weeks from opening a bricks-and-mortar cafe with a business partner. Also holds a degree in nutritional medicine / nutritional therapy which he has never practised. On his feet all day; works roughly 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. with no days off at present. Self-employed for three years, no sick pay.
prospect.family_status: Has a girlfriend / partner, lives with a Hungarian Vizsla, no children. His cat was killed two weeks before the call.
prospect.training_background: Trained heavily through his twenties and thirties — half marathons, weights, wakeboarding. Last thirteen years have been inconsistent: 'so many gym memberships, two personal trainers, loads of different physios.' Took up kettlebells about two and a half to three years ago with an American online coach named Colin (Flow), training five days a week; leaned out fast, burned out and stopped. Then trained at a private members gym in Guildford in small groups of six to eight for October to December, felt great, and stopped in January after badly injuring his shoulder. Has done essentially nothing for about eighteen months beyond walking the dog, stretching, and foot work with toe spacers and lacrosse balls. Owns kettlebells already — one 8kg, two 16s, two 20s, two 24s.
prospect.medical: Right shoulder: ultrasound showed the right bursa almost twice the size of the left, with impingement pinching the bicep tendon and presenting initially as bicep tendonitis. Had a steroid injection at his GP and reacted badly — severe lower leg cramps, no pain relief, about two months to settle. A repeat ultrasound still showed swelling; he declined the proposed ultrasound-guided injection, saying 'effectively, steroids is poison.' Currently doing rehab with a physiotherapist friend. Present limitations: pull-ups are a no-no, hanging is a no-no, 'can't really lift much above my shoulder confidently', and the right shoulder is markedly less mobile than the left. Also: left hip plays up; roughly six months of tennis elbow managed with rice buckets, squeeze balls and bands; slipped a couple of discs in a workplace back accident in his thirties and had epidurals; late thirties spent in and out of injury including crutches and ruptured ligaments. A previous episode of burnout with rapid unintended body-fat and weight loss when training five days a week. An osteopath he knows told him 'I don't think training really suits you.' Wakes stiff, particularly in the legs. Sleep described as okay but wobbling under business stress. Currently 74kg at roughly six foot.

signals: Eighteen months of ground lost squarely to injury, and he dates it precisely: 'It's nearly a year and a half ago, and I've pretty much not done much since'
Wants the former self back and says the age is not the barrier: 'I don't feel like just because I'm the age I'm at that I'm not capable of getting my fitness back'
Loud, explicit regret and self-directed anger — 'I'm probably quite hard on myself', and the success image is 'I might actually smile at myself and thank myself instead of calling myself an idiot'
Names the pattern himself: 'it's stop, start, stop, start, stop... over time, it's just become too easy to just then get too comfortable'

OVERLAP NOTE: the_preserver fits several dimensions unusually well — 53, genuinely health-literate with a nutritional therapy degree, already under physiotherapy care, and a business owner whose income is real but whose discretionary liquidity is near zero because everything is going into the new premises. He is assigned rebuilder rather than preserver because his stated goal is recovery of a lost capacity, not retention of a current one.

goals.text: Consistency above everything else — 'if we could fast forward a year and I am consistent with it, and a year later I've progressed because I've been consistent, I think that would be the main thing'
Crack the shoulder and the other niggles and find out what his body can actually still do
Feel stronger and get his mobility back so his joints move properly
Be less likely to be injured — injury prevention is the explicit outcome he names
More energy and a clearer head — 'I know that training will help clear my head'
Change his relationship with himself — stop calling himself an idiot and start thanking himself
Learn it well enough to carry it independently into his sixties, seventies and eighties
Show up better for his partner, his business partner and his customers — 'she would hear less of me moaning'
Train at home rather than at a gym, which he has tried and which does not work for him

pains.text: Right shoulder bursitis and impingement, ultrasound-confirmed, which rules out pull-ups, hanging and confident overhead lifting
Adverse reaction to a steroid injection — severe lower leg cramps, no pain relief, two months to settle — leaving him unwilling to accept the offered follow-up injection
Eighteen months of near-total inactivity, the longest layoff of his life
Thirteen years of stop-start — multiple gym memberships, two personal trainers, many physios, nothing that held
Previous burnout from training five days a week, with rapid unintended loss of body fat and weight in a man who already carries none
An osteopath he knows and trusts told him training does not suit him
Fear of re-injury compounded by self-employment with no sick pay — 'I don't want to get injured again. I work for myself now, I have to go to work, I don't get sick pay'

Distrust of remote coaching after Colin/Flow — 'how do they really see what you're doing? I can leave this call now and go in the next room and think I'm doing snatches right, and I'm not, and I'm just going to hurt myself again'
Cash locked up in the new premises — 'we've been earning relatively just enough to cover our bills for the last kind of six months'
No time and no appetite for a gym; he wants to train at home and has tried the alternative
Emotional volatility and short patience when he is fatigued, which leaks into work — 'if I'm feeling off, if something's bothering me, then people know about it'
Eating pattern collapsing under the business build — long involuntary fasts, skipped meals, pastries at work, more bread than usual
Wakes stiff, legs suffering; sleep wobbling under contractor and opening stress
Grief — his cat was killed two weeks before the call and the dog is unsettled by it
Previous programme was too time-costly to follow — sessions meant to take 30-45 minutes took him an hour and twenty

objections.raw_quote: I am dubious about online coaching, because I kind of do, I sometimes think to myself, well, how do they really see what you're doing? How do you get that extra kind of care that you might need if you're trying to come in at it with some mobility issues? And, you know, I can leave this call now and go in the next room and think I'm doing snatches right, and I'm not, and I'm just going to hurt myself again.
objections.rep_response: Did not address it at the time. Later described the weekly film-and-review loop and, when the concern resurfaced during pillar one, added the light-weight progression reassurance

objections.raw_quote: I saw another physio who I know quite well, and he actually did say to me... I don't think training really suits you.
objections.rep_response: 'I'm just going to be direct with you, that's rubbish.'

objections.raw_quote: one thing I've never, never really got on with is fasting... I've tried fasting before. I've really struggled with that. So it's something I would be interested to look at again, but it's not suited me at all at any point in me trying it.
objections.rep_response: 'especially as we, if we're over 40, fasting, introducing fasting protocols to what you're doing, it directly contributes to having longevity for yourself' and 'Trevor's here to kind of correct that for yourself. We should, we have the capacity to fast.'

objections.raw_quote: I'm probably, given my financial situation at the moment, and knowing where my credit card's at, I probably would do the trial... I won't be able to commit to the six or 12. I just don't have the funds for that.
objections.rep_response: Thanked him for the honesty, explained the differential upgrade mechanic, and then actively recommended the cheapest option: 'if I was just telling you what to do, just do the one month. Don't do the three.'

objections.raw_quote: There is a wobble there. As soon as you said that, there's the doubt pops in... I'm like, Oh, am I? Can I? Can I actually do it?
objections.rep_response: 'Good. It's meant to be there.' Then framed the doubt as fear and moved to price within two minutes without returning to the consequence frame

objections.raw_quote: I need to sleep on it... I just need some time to process it all, really. I just want some time away from the call just to sit down and have a cup of chamomile tea, chill out a bit.
objections.rep_response: Asked one probe — 'what else do you kind of need to think of before making your decision?' — accepted the answer and booked a follow-up for Wednesday

objections.raw_quote: where is Trevor, is he California or somewhere?
objections.rep_response: Confirmed Sacramento and noted the client base is US first, then UK, then Netherlands and Dubai

offer.payment_plan_terms: Mentioned only in passing — 'most people just put it on a credit card, but we have a couple of payment plan options if necessary.' Nothing was structured. The differential upgrade mechanic was explained in detail: coming in at the $1,200 trial and moving to three months costs $2,800 rather than $4,000.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Asked directly what happens in the event of injury, the rep answered 'Full refund.' followed by 'that's the only case where we need to stop things, of course. Life happens, you know, you break your leg or whatever.'

evidence: No payment and no decision. He declined explicitly and pre-emptively: 'I wouldn't make a decision now. And I think if you tried to get me to, I'd probably say, all right, I won't do it. Then I'd probably just go.'
A second call was booked, confirmed and accepted into his calendar — Wednesday 8 p.m. UK time, with the invite verified live: 'I've got it. I've added it to Google Calendar.'
Leaning clearly toward the $1,200 one-month trial: 'It'd have to be that one, I think... probably more likely to be the trial one', and the rep endorsed that choice
Intent is high and the trust gauge answer was strong — 'I do think I need it. I don't think I would have wasted your time or mine booking the call'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: an unresolved capability wobble was surfaced at 00:52:49 and never worked through, and the affordability constraint is structural — business cash is committed to a fit-out for at least the near term
outcome.next_step: Second call booked for Wednesday 8 p.m. UK time; prospect to sit with the decision and most likely take the $1,200 one-month trial

notable.note: Two things dominate this record. First, the file is titled for a completely different person — 'Jaideep Mistry' appears nowhere in the transcript, and the entire call is with Paul Hatch. Second, this is the most heavily injured prospect in the batch and the rep dismissed a named clinician's advice to his face: told that an osteopath he knows well had said training does not suit him, the rep answered 'I'm just going to be direct with you, that's rubbish.' The prospect has an ultrasound-confirmed right bursa nearly twice the size of the left, cannot hang or lift confidently overhead, reacted badly to a steroid injection and refused the follow-up, has slipped discs and epidurals in his history, and previously burned out training five days a week with unintended weight loss at 74kg. The rep also pushed fasting on him after he said plainly it has never suited him — 'Trevor's here to kind of correct that for yourself' — to a 53-year-old already going 16 to 19 hours without food on physically demanding workdays. Against all of that, the same rep ran the best Baseline in this entire folder, probed the shoulder history properly, and honestly steered him to the cheapest tier rather than pushing the six or twelve. The competence is real; the clinical guardrails are absent.

quality.notes: Among the worst in the batch — the labels invert for long continuous runs, so entire rep monologues sit under 'Paul Hatch' and vice versa. Unambiguous examples: the whole of pillar three's delivery at 00:44:28 to 00:44:35 alternates mid-sentence; 'Does that all make sense, Paul?' at 00:45:02 is labelled Paul Hatch; 'I had a steroid injection in my shoulder at the local doctors, and I had a really bad reaction to it' at 00:05:07 is labelled Farooq Bey but is plainly the prospect's medical history; 'I'm just going to be direct with you, that's rubbish' at 00:22:32 is labelled Farooq Bey and is correct, but the surrounding turns are not. Roles were resolved from content throughout. The prospect's email and full mobile number are captured verbatim in the transcript at 01:05:12.
